place.source_title: Cerealine Manufacturing Company, Mill A, Jackson & Brown Streets

brief: The town's original riverside mill: a four-storey brick block with pilastered walls, tall round-arched windows set in recessed panels, a shallow hipped roof and a single chimney, with a lower loading wing at the back. The founding flour mill of Harrow Falls, converted to loft apartments; ivy covers one end wall and a parking lot replaces the old wagon yard.

facade.notes: Cerealine Mill A (Columbus IN, c.1880), HAER: a four-storey brick mill with pilastered walls, round-arched windows in recessed panels (some bricked up), a shallow metal hip roof and a chimney; ivy; a low concrete-block shed and a Quonset-roofed shed beside it; bare gravel yard

why.note: before electric motors and steel frames, a factory was a narrow tall masonry block: daylight from both sides, power from one line shaft or a waterwheel
